ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the tangent to circle $O$ at point $A$, $OB$ intersects circle $O$ at point $C$, point $D$ is on circle $O$, and $AD$, $CD$, $OA$ are connected. If $\angle ADC = 25^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ADC=25^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle AOC=50^\circ$,\\
since $AB$ is a tangent of $\odot O$ at point A,\\
thus, $\angle OAB=90^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle B=90^\circ-\angle AOC=90^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

OA is the radius from the center O to the point of tangency A. The oblique line OB starts from B, passes through point C on the circle, and reaches O, indicating that B, C, O are collinear. Reasoning: A, C, D are all on circle O, and ∠ADC is an inscribed angle formed by chords AD and CD. OA is the radius from the center O to the point of tangency A. The oblique line OB starts from B, passes through point C on the circle, and reaches O, indicating that B, C, O are collinear. Point D is at the lower right of the circle, AD and CD are connected, forming the inscribed angle ∠ADC.

Reasoning: A, C, D are all on circle O, and ∠ADC is an inscribed angle formed by chords AD and CD. It is known that ∠ADC = 25°, and the central angle corresponding to its subtended arc AC is ∠AOC, therefore ∠AOC = 2 × 25° = 50°. Since B, C, O are collinear, ray OB and OC are on the same straight line, ∠AOB = ∠AOC = 50°. Also because AB is the tangent to circle O at point A, and OA is the radius to the point of tangency A, therefore OA ⟂ AB, that is, ∠OAB = 90°. In triangle AOB, ∠B = 180° − 90° − 50° = 40°.
